Four more women are waiting for us

Each one is a gem through which the white light of pre-messianic femininity refracts into her own colours and hues, to escort us on our own journeys, and to convert our suffering to love, our challenges to victories, our exiles into our redemption.

Semester 1

The Dina Semester

Rise! into Feminine Influence

She’s the seventh child of Yaakov after six boys, daughter of Leah Imeinu. Who is this little girl, Dina? She’s the lost princess, of course. Everything that happens to her happens to the cosmic feminine as she rises.

The Tamar Semester

Rise! into Holy Femininity

Daughter of Shem, wife of Yehuda, she is none other than the mother of Mashiach. Her story holds the secrets of Mashiach.

Semester 3

The Miriam Semester

Rise! into Feminine Leadership

The second of the seven prophetesses, sister of Moshe and Aaron, shepherdess of a newborn nation, midwife, healer, influencer and guide. If anyone will lead us out of this exile, it is she.

Semester 4

The Daughters of Tzelafchad Semester

Rise! into Malchus

Machlah, Noah, Choglah, Milcah and Tirzah: five extra-ordinary, righteous, knowledge-seeking women. Through them we forge and seal our connection to Shabbos, the Shechina, and our holy feminine power.

Learn it your way

Every class is recorded, so you can learn whenever it suits you. Around the recordings there is room to talk it through, share it and go deeper alongside other women, including an Ask Rebbetzin Tamar event each semester. All of it is optional.

On your own

The recorded classes, the source sheets, and a one-page companion for each class: a takeaway, three questions and one vessel exercise.

In a pod

Opt in to a small pod of Rise! II women, matched by time zone. Every class comes with a sheet to open with, and a mentor to oversee, b’ezras Hashem.

In a live circle

Small live circles with the mentors, a held space for vessel work, to bring what you learned into your life. Optional.

From women who have walked Rise! II

Do you remember the last session of Rise! I?

That full, quiet, slightly strange feeling when it was over… You had walked through Chava and Sarah, Rivka, Rachel and Leah. You had sat with the vessel work, and maybe you’d even watched some of the creases in your life begin to iron themselves out. You were grateful. And somewhere underneath the gratitude, a small voice said, “wait… there’s more.”

And since then? Maybe your days have felt a little different. Quieter. You miss the weekly stimulation, that thread of learning running underneath the laundry and the lunches.

That voice was telling you the truth. 💛

Rise! I was the preparing of the ground and the building of the foundations. The mystery of women in the Torah is so delicious that perhaps Hashem saved it as one of the last secrets to be revealed before the coming of Mashiach. And once you’ve tasted a little of it, it’s hard to pretend it isn’t there.

It is with this unearned gift and merit that we will once again enter into the “Palace of the King” to find our true place in His world, and see how we can Rise! into this holy feminine at the end of days.

All my love, Tamar

Deeper. Much deeper.

You have known these women all your life. Dina. Tamar. Miriam. The daughters of Tzelafchad. But what if you never really understood them?

Each one is a world: a spiritual microcosm, a whole inner universe, and at the same time a macrocosm, a story that reaches all the way to the Jewish people and to redemption. Rebbetzin Tamar takes you underneath the story you thought you knew, to the hidden Torah and wisdom waiting there.

And then they come home with you. Who these women really were, and what that says about who you are. How they show up in your marriage, your mothering, your friendships, your reactions on an ordinary day. You carry on learning, and it keeps changing how you live.

Rise! I taught you the beauty and power of the feminine. Rise! II brings everything together: the feminine and the masculine, light and vessel, the big picture and the moment you’re standing in. It’s deeper, and it’s more practical, too, than you might expect.

This is the kind of learning that makes you stop and ask, “Wait… it was there the whole time?”

It quenches the thirst. And you keep on learning.

The women who love Rise don’t love it only because it’s deep. They love it because it feeds them. Every class leaves you nourished, and a little more thirsty for the next.

Stories you may never have understood

Women you thought you knew turn out to be so much more. You begin to see your own story inside theirs, and to understand who you are, and why, on a deeper level.

How they live in your life

What you learn reaches into your marriage, your children, your friendships and your relationship with Hashem. Women tell us they catch themselves reacting differently, with more peace and a little of the holy chutzpah Rebbetzin Tamar teaches.

A thirst quenched, and a thirst for more

Learning that feeds the soul and the mind at once. Women tell us they finish a class full, and still wanting more. This is the next course of that meal.

From women in Rise! I

Is it for me?

So many of us walk around thinking we’re the only one. The only one who’s thirsty for this. The only one with these questions. And then one day we find a group of women, and something loosens. We are not alone. We never were.

Rise! II is for women who have already walked Rise! I with me. Women who know the language of Rise!, who don’t need the paradigms explained, who are ready to go deeper and happy to do it together.

“Am I ready?” You are. We don’t begin from the beginning. We begin from where you stand, and we go deeper.

“Do I have the time?” Every class is a recording, so you learn when it suits you, and there is a pause between each semester to catch up. You don’t have to show up perfectly. You just have to keep showing up. And if you’d like company, the support is there.

“I was pregnant and was afraid I won’t manage with a little newborn. But I’m glad I joined. It actually worked out pretty well with all the breaks in between.” GZ, NY

“Be gentle with yourself. You don’t have to understand every deep piece of it. Just go with the flow and your soul will pick up what it needs.” Esther Yenty Noe, Monsey NY

Yes. Come on in.
